arxiv-2012-12615.title: Probabilistic Iterative Methods for Linear Systems
arxiv-2012-12615.creator: Jon Cockayne, Ilse C.F. Ipsen, Chris J. Oates, Tim W. Reid
arxiv-2012-12615.description: Abstract This paper presents a probabilistic perspective on iterative methods for approximating the solution 𝐱 ∈ ℝ d \mathbf{x}\in\mathbb{R}^{d} of a nonsingular linear system 𝐀𝐱 = 𝐛 \mathbf{A}\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b} . Classically, an iterative method produces a sequence 𝐱 m \mathbf{x}_{m} of approximations that converge to 𝐱 \mathbf{x} in ℝ d \mathbb{R}^{d} .

arxiv-2306-16079.title: On Card guessing games: limit law for one-time riffle shuffle
arxiv-2306-16079.creator: Markus Kuba, Alois Panholzer
arxiv-2306-16079.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Markus Kuba, Alois Panholzer. We consider a card guessing game with complete feedback. A ordered deck of n n cards labeled 1 1 up to n n is riffle-shuffled exactly one time. Then, the goal of the game is to maximize the number of correct guesses of the cards, where one after another a single card is drawn from the top, and shown to the guesser until no cards remain. Improving earlier results, we provide a limit law for the number of correct guesses.

arxiv-2308-02182.title: AutoML4ETC: Automated Neural Architecture Search for Real-World Encrypted Traffic Classification
arxiv-2308-02182.creator: Navid Malekghaini 1 , Elham Akbari 1 , Mohammad A. Salahuddin 1 , Noura Limam 1 , Raouf Boutaba 1 , Bertrand Mathieu 2 , Stephanie Moteau 2 , and Stephane Tuffin 2
arxiv-2308-02182.description: Abstract Deep learning (DL) has been successfully applied to encrypted network traffic classification in experimental settings. However, in production use, it has been shown that a DL classifier’s performance inevitably decays over time. Re-training the model on newer datasets has been shown to only partially improve its performance.

arxiv-2310-13961.title: Ensemble-Instruct: Generating Instruction-Tuning Data with a Heterogeneous Mixture of LMs
arxiv-2310-13961.creator: Young-Suk Lee, Md Arafat Sultan, Yousef El-Kurdi, Tahira Naseem
arxiv-2310-13961.description: Abstract Using in-context learning (ICL) for data generation, techniques such as Self-Instruct Wang et al. 2023 or the follow-up Alpaca Taori et al. 2023 can train strong conversational agents with only a small amount of human supervision. One limitation of these approaches is that they resort to very large language models (around 175B parameters) that are also proprietary and non-public.

arxiv-2312-11653.title: Self-dual toric varieties Thanks: Corresponding author: Apostolos Thoma
arxiv-2312-11653.creator: Apostolos Thoma, Marius Vladoiu
arxiv-2312-11653.description: Abstract . We describe explicitly all multisets of weights whose defining projective toric varieties are self-dual. In addition, we describe a remarkable and unexpected combinatorial behaviour of the defining ideals of these varieties. The toric ideal of a self-dual projective variety is weakly robust, that means the Graver basis is the union of all minimal binomial generating sets.

arxiv-2401-15306.creator: Alireza Abdollahi a , Majid Arezoomand b , Tao Feng c and Shixin Wang c a Department of Pure Mathematics, Faculty of Mathematics and Statistics, University of Isfahan, Isfahan 81746-73441, Iran b University of Larestan, Larestan 74317-16137, Iran b Department of Mathematics, Faculty of Science, Shah
arxiv-2401-15306.description: Abstract In this paper, we introduce the concept of k k -integral graphs. A graph Γ \Gamma is called k k -integral if the extension degree of the splitting field of the characteristic polynomial of Γ \Gamma over rational field ℚ \mathbb{Q} is equal to k k .

arxiv-2409-08788.title: Electrocardiogram Report Generation and Question Answering via Retrieval-Augmented Self-Supervised Modeling
arxiv-2409-08788.creator: Jialu Tang 1 , Tong Xia 2 , Yuan Lu 1 , Cecilia Mascolo 2 , Aaqib Saeed 1
arxiv-2409-08788.description: Abstract Interpreting electrocardiograms (ECGs) and generating comprehensive reports remain challenging tasks in cardiology, often requiring specialized expertise and significant time investment. To address these critical issues, we propose ECG-ReGen, a retrieval-based approach for ECG-to-text report generation and question answering. Our method leverages a self-supervised learning for the ECG encoder, enabling efficient similarity searches and report retrieval.

arxiv-2502-01253.title: Explainability-Driven Quality Assessment for Rule-Based Systems
arxiv-2502-01253.creator: Oshani Seneviratne, Brendan Capuzzo, William Van Woensel
arxiv-2502-01253.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Oshani Seneviratne, Brendan Capuzzo, William Van Woensel. This paper introduces an explanation framework designed to enhance the quality of rules in knowledge-based reasoning systems based on dataset-driven insights. The traditional method for rule induction from data typically requires labor-intensive labeling and data-driven learning. This framework provides an alternative and instead allows for the data-driven refinement of existing rules: it generates explanations of rule inferences and leverages human interpretation to refine rules.

arxiv-2508-06391.title: Improved Dysarthric Speech to Text Conversion via TTS Personalization Thanks: This work was supported by the Hungarian NRDI Fund through projects NKFIH K143075/K135038, NKFIH-828-2/2021 and by KIFÜ Kommondor.
arxiv-2508-06391.creator: Péter Mihajlik 1 3 , Éva Székely 2 , Piroska Barta 1 , Máté Soma Kádár 3 4 , Gergely Dobsinszki 4 1 , László Tóth 5
arxiv-2508-06391.description: Abstract We present a case study on developing a customized speech-to-text system for a Hungarian speaker with severe dysarthria. State-of-the-art automatic speech recognition (ASR) models struggle with zero-shot transcription of dysarthric speech, yielding high error rates. To improve performance with limited real dysarthric data, we fine-tune an ASR model using synthetic speech generated via a personalized text-to-speech (TTS) system.

pmc-11302264.title: Measurable therapeutic antibody in serum as potential predictive factor of response to anti-CD38 therapy in non-IgG-k myeloma patients
pmc-11302264.creator: Emilia Gigliotta, Federica Plano, Giusy Corsale, Anna Maria Corsale, Cristina Aquilina, Maria Speciale, Andrea Rizzuto, Enrica Antonia Martino, Dario Leotta, Antonio Giovanni Solimando, Roberto Ria, Massimo Gentile, Sergio Siragusa, Cirino Botta
pmc-11302264.description: Multiple myeloma (MM) is a hematologic malignancy characterized by abnormal plasma cell proliferation in the bone marrow. Recent advancements in anti-CD38 monoclonal antibody therapies, such as daratumumab and isatuximab, have significantly improved MM patient survival. However, the lack of predictive factors of response to these therapies remains a challenge. Notably, anti-CD38 antibodies can interfere with laboratory tests, complicating response assessment.

pmc-11458895.title: Bio-printing method as a novel approach to obtain a fibrin scaffold settled by limbal epithelial cells for corneal regeneration
pmc-11458895.creator: Krzysztof Pietryga, Katarzyna Jesse, Rafał Drzyzga, Adam Konka, Joanna Zembala-John, Aleksandra Kowalik, Zdzisław Kiełbowicz, Marek Ćwirko, Rafał J Bułdak, Dariusz Dobrowolski, Edward Wylęgała
pmc-11458895.description: Treatment of Limbal Stem Cell Deficiency (LSCD), based on autologous transplantation of the patient’s stem cells, is one of the few medical stem cell therapies approved by the European Medicines Agency (EMA). It relies on isolating and culturing in vivo Limbal Epithelial Stem Cells (LESC) and then populating them on the fibrin substrate, creating a scaffold for corneal epithelial regeneration.

pmc-12452498.title: A Retrospective Study of Cefiderocol Utilization and Associated Outcomes at an Academic Medical Center
pmc-12452498.creator: Samantha G. Rauch, Michelle H. Potter, Emir Kobic
pmc-12452498.description: Background: This study aimed to describe cefiderocol prescription and associated patient outcomes at a U.S. academic medical center for various multidrug-resistant organisms (MDRO). pmc-12565932.title: Atomistic Doping Effects on the Ideal Strength of Graphene/Aluminum Interfaces
pmc-12565932.creator: Wei Wang, Can Cui, Fangfang Xia, Weiwei Xu, Tieqiang Gang, Lijie Chen, Jan Haubrich
pmc-12565932.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Generally, atomic doping is an effective method to address the weak bonding strength of the graphene/aluminum (Gr/Al) composite interface structure caused by physical adsorption, thereby enhancing the mechanical properties of the interface structure. In this paper, the nanoscopic influence mechanisms of atomic (M, including 12 types of atoms (elements)) doping in the aluminum matrix (Al) on the ideal strength of the Gr/Al interface structures are investigated based on density functional theory.

pmc-13173123.title: 152 Lessons and experiences in recruitment and retention challenges from the Alzheimer’s disease progression after stroke study (ADAPT-MRI)
pmc-13173123.creator: Ruth Yanes Bengoa, Prasen Marella, Heather Smith, Andrew Barreto, Sean Savitz, Fadi Musfee
pmc-13173123.description: Objectives/Goals: Stroke and Alzheimer’s disease (AD) often co-occur. The ADAPT-MRI study faced major enrollment challenges while assessing stroke’s impact on AD. This analysis examined recruitment and retention barriers in enrolling adults with early cognitive impairment and recent stroke for a longitudinal imaging study.

pmc-13615553.title: The Role of S100A8/A9 in Autoimmune Eye Diseases: From Pathogenesis to Targeted Therapy
pmc-13615553.creator: Tingyu Zhang, Jiangqi Hu, Mei Sun, Xinyu Zhang, Hui Xu, Bei Du, Yankai Wei, Ruihua Wei
pmc-13615553.description: The S100 proteins are a group of calcium-binding proteins that are widely expressed in vertebrates and participate in various biological and pathological processes, including cell proliferation, differentiation, inflammation, infection, and autoimmunity. S100A8 and S100A9, members of the S100 family that predominantly exist as heterodimers (S100A8/A9), are primarily localized in myeloid cells such as neutrophils, monocytes, and dendritic cells (DCs).
